title: Meeting the developer at the error
hook: Why does an "Ask Kiro to Fix" quick fix matter more than it sounds?

back.lead: Kiro added an editor context submenu, a guided form for creating hooks, and an **Ask Kiro to Fix** quick fix on errors and warnings. Individually those are conveniences. Together they move the agent from a panel you switch to into the place the problem already is — and the distance between noticing a defect and asking for help is most of what decides whether anyone asks.

kv.v: The agent appears on the squiggle, in the context menu, and in a form — at the point of the problem, rather than in a chat you have to go and find.

kv.k: Why a guided form for hooks
kv.v: A hook is powerful and easy to get subtly wrong. A form is an admission that the blank file was the barrier, and that discoverability beats expressiveness for a feature most people never enable.

Convenience at the error site raises how often an agent is invoked on small things. That is the intent, and it is also where an unreviewed suggestion is most likely to be accepted without reading — the same reason a quick fix is useful.

back.hookline: The agent that gets used is the one already where you are looking. That is also the one whose output you skim.

history.reason: Authored to close an actionable check-coverage gap: the Kiro changelog entry this card covers matched no existing card's subject. New cards are Tier C by definition.
